newsitem.title: USA: Calif. importers charged with food-smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Calif. importers charged with food-smuggling.

text.p: Federal agents have arrested eight owners or former owners of northern California companies on charges of smuggling adulterated food products into the United States, prosecutors said on Friday.
The arrests, made on Thursday and on Friday, followed a 10-month investigation led by the U.S. Customs Service, the U.S. Attorney's Office for northern California said.
The government alleged that the importers conspired to smuggle 40-foot containers of foods, mainly Asian seafood, into the United States without the necessary health and safety inspections.
The importers bribed officials of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and U.S. Customs brokers, prosecutors alleged.

During the undercover operation, federal agents videotaped meetings at which importers negotiated to smuggle foods into the United States without undergoing inspection by FDA officials designed to prevent tainted foods from entering the United States, prosecutors said.

"The investigation was designed to protect the health and safety of American consumers from products which are unsafe, filthy, or produced under unsanitary conditions," the U.S. Attorney's office said in a statement.
The statement did not make clear whether the importers succeeded in bringing any of the products into the United States.

Indictments have also been filed under court seal against at least two FDA inspectors and at least two U.S. Customs brokers accused of accepting bribes, a spokesman for the U.S. attorney's office said.

Nayseap Hong and Lang Nang, owners of the Royal Food Trading Co. of San Jose, California; and Willie Hong, owner of GLC Trading of Hayward, California. were charged with conspiracy to smuggle goods into the United States.

Kevin Choy and Eric Sit, owners of Pacific Rim Seafood of Oakland, California; George Lai, owner of TM Trading of San Francisco; and Edison Gabriel and Raymond Lau, former owners of U.S. Pacific Rim of San Leandro, California, were charged with conspiracy to smuggle goods into the United States and bribery of public officials.

Each conspiracy count carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine. The bribery charge carries a maximum penalty of 15 years in prison and a fine of three times the value of the bribe or $250,000.
The importers were all granted release on a $50,000 secured bond at a hearing before a federal magistrate in San Francisco on Friday.
